How did you make the dress form? What stuffing did you use?

It's based on a 5-panel fitted bodice but has an extra 6 inches of length. This way of drafting fitted bodices is no longer used or taught, unfortunately. I found instructions in a public domain book on dressmaking.

The awesome thing about this form of drafting is the spectacular fit especially across the shoulders. It's also based on real measures. Some modern drafting methods don't work well with real measures and require lots of later adjustments.

The stuffing is just plain old cheap poly-fill. I had thought I would need to weight it down and would need to put something heavy on the bottom but turns out, the form is very balanced and can sit up on it's own.

Now, I can display things!

1 yard of 60" canvas and 2 1/2 bags of poly-fill. Neck, armholes and bottom all had to be hand sewn. Form is a 35-30-36. Corset is Edwardian S-Front.
